speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of painful urination, and a history of a similar painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or fever accompanying the knee swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome).

The combination of a recent asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle then knee), urethritis (painful urination), and a young male patient with inconsistent condom use strongly suggests Reactive Arthritis triggered by a sexually transmitted infection, likely Chlamydia. Given the "can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree" presentation, further testing is not required for a clinical decision in this classic case.
